meta.purpose: exp77 pre-freeze PASS 1 (working file, NOT of record): reproduction of the committed CAMeL root/pattern extraction over the 519 D4 inventory + the 24 HUMANS

pipeline_reused.root_pattern_source: the admitting analysis, i.e. the first Al_det definite NOUN reading with rat='r', gen='m', num='s' -- extract_aravec_candidates.py:321-322

rows.note_committed: Human ('the Westerner/foreigner'), but colloquial-Egyptian and now somewhat dated; ta-marbuta form.

Extremely common family name and a club name (المصري البورسعيدي), but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (the nationality reading dominates). Wazn tag mu_participle is an error; it is a nisba.

Egyptian family name (عصام العريان was prominent in the corpus era), but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept ('naked' is fully live in Egyptian usage).
Base form; الاخو (also in the inventory) is its non-standard variant.
Near-duplicate of اليماني (also in the inventory); اليمني is the ordinary nationality form.
Human as a military rank/title (اللواء فلان) but also 'brigade' and, in Jordan, an administrative district.
Orthographic duplicate of الاميركي (also in the inventory).
Older ethnic term for the same referent as الاثيوبي (also in the inventory); also a common family name.
Hamza-variant duplicate of المسؤول (also in the inventory); same word, both kept only because both are AraVec vocabulary types.
Kept because the bare person-noun use is genuinely common (سياسي بارز، المحلل السياسي), unlike الفني/الاقتصادي; but the adjective 'political' is also frequent.
Dialectal participle 'drowned/soaked'; applies to people but also to soaked objects.
Human (Egyptian slur for an effeminate or passive homosexual man); extremely vulgar.
Human ('young man') but also the adjective 'young' and, unvocalised, الشَّبّ 'alum'.

Given name and family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (الأمين العام 'secretary-general' is highly frequent); also a divine-adjacent epithet.
Ta-marbuta written as ه; equals الطاغية 'tyrant', and is a near-duplicate of الطاغي (also in the inventory). Human but wazn-tagged nisba_yaa in error.
Human, but in practice a rigid designator for the Prophet rather than a generic 'messenger' referent slot.

Common Gulf family name and part of الخلفاء الراشدون, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept ('adult, of sound judgement' is live in legal/medical talk).
Broken plural 'sheikhs' — human, but violates the masculine-singular convention of the inventory.

Family name (Al-Issawi), but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (follower of Jesus); low currency as a descriptor.
Also a divine name and a military rank; the human 'observer/censor/sergeant' readings are live.
Human ('brother') but also the diplomatic adjective for states (البلد الشقيق).
Human honorific title; Ottoman-era and now colloquial address.
Human 'friend', but also the epithet of Abu Bakr (أبو بكر الصديق), which inflates its frequency.
Denotes an Umayyad person, but dominant Twitter use is attributive to non-humans (الدولة الأموية، المسجد الأموي).
Human ('newborn') but also the passive participle 'born' and the Prophet's مولد derivatives.
Also a divine name; human readings ('sage', and in dialect 'the doctor') are live, and it is a prominent Iraqi family name.
Orthographic duplicate of الانكليزي and الانقليزي, both also in the inventory.
Also a divine name (al-Mu'min), but the human 'believer' reading is overwhelmingly dominant on Twitter.
Dialectal form of الرئيس; human, colloquial (boss/skipper).
Also part of the divine formula نعم المولى ونعم النصير; the human 'supporter' reading survives, and it is a given name.
Human nationality nisba (wazn tag mu_participle is an error); also collides with المغرب 'sunset/Maghrib prayer' derivatives and is a common family name.
Nationality form; contrast البحراني (also in the inventory), which in usage denotes Bahraini Shia specifically.
Human ('the stranger') but the discourse use والغريب أن and the adjective 'strange' of things are at least as frequent.
Non-standard written form of الاب (also in the inventory), from أبو-constructions; human but orthographically defective.
Human ('individual') but also 'a single unit' of non-humans, and 'a pistol' in some dialects.
Family name and tribal nisba (بنو هلال), but on Gulf Twitter dominantly 'an Al-Hilal club supporter' — still a human referent.

Family name (very common), but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept ('preacher/orator', and dialectal 'fiance').
Human ('old person') but frequently female-referring in dialect and pejorative.
Broken plural 'dervishes' — human, but plural; also a nickname for Zamalek/Ahli fan groups in Egyptian football talk.
Human ('intruder, outsider') but also the linguistic 'loanword' (لفظ دخيل); also a family name.
Human ('member' of a body) but also the anatomical 'organ'.
Orthographic duplicate of الامريكي (also in the inventory).

Common given/family name (and a Sudanese/Egyptian surname), but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept ('the good/kind one' is live); homograph with الطيب 'perfume'.
Gulf 'religious enforcer / Quran teacher'; human, regionally marked.
Base form; الابو (also in the inventory) is its non-standard variant.
Orthographic duplicate of الاوربي and الاروبي, both also in the inventory.
Human (preacher/propagandist); ta-marbuta form, and the CAMeL gloss also lists a non-human 'motive' reading.
Human ('cashier, money changer') but competes with the very frequent الصراف الآلي 'ATM'.
Human ('guardian, saint, patron') but also the divine name الولي and abstract 'authority' (ولي الأمر).
Human as 'unidentified person' but equally 'unknown quantity/thing' (ضد مجهول، المجهول).
Human, but note two live senses: 'client/customer' (commercial) and 'collaborator/agent' (political slur).
Human ('guardian/trustee'); legal role term, and the Shia theological الوصي.
Egyptian 'beggar' (human) and also a common Egyptian family name.
Human only inside the frozen idiom اختلط الحابل بالنابل; no independent referential use.
Human ('shepherd, patron, sponsor') but also a well-known Saudi dairy brand.
Gulf dialect plural/collective 'old men' as well as the tribal name شيبان; human but not a masculine singular.
Plural of كريم used of people (الضيوف الكرام) — human, but plural and formulaic.
Refers to a woman ('the lady', Egyptian ست); female referent despite the inventory's masculine convention, and also the fixed epithet of Umm Kulthum.
Plural 'infidels' — human, but plural; heavily polemical register.
Also a divine name (al-Warith); the human 'heir' reading is live in legal and everyday talk.
Family name and scholarly nisba (الحسن البصري), but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (from Basra).
Human ('a leading figure', قيادي في الحزب) but also an ordinary adjective 'leadership-related'.
Human ('Caesar/tsar') but also an epithet (قيصر الغناء) and a codename (قانون قيصر).
Non-standard written form of الاخ (also in the inventory), from dialectal/construct spellings; human but orthographically defective.
Human as 'eloquent speaker', but the adjective mostly modifies speech and effects (الأثر البليغ).
Human ('maternal uncle') but also 'mole/beauty spot' (خال) in poetry.
Human (الفتى 'youth') but the alif-maqsura is written as ya, and فَتِيّ 'youthful/strong' is a homograph.
Hamza-less spelling of القارئ 'reader' (also in the inventory); the CAMeL gloss 'villager' is a spurious قروي reading.
Egyptian 'bullshitter/braggart' and the trade 'lathe turner'; human, colloquial.
Rare 'father-in-law'; the bare definite spelling is largely a fragment/noise on Twitter.
Evaluative adjective 'peerless', used attributively of persons (قائد فذ); human-applying but not a referent noun on its own.
Dialectal 'thief'; human, colloquial.
Human ('the one who calls/invites', الداعي إلى الله) with strong Quranic support; kept, but the abstract 'reason' sense exists (though the frequent لا داعي lacks the article).
Alif-maqsura written as ya (الأعمى). Human, but the spelling is defective.
Human as 'dutiful/pious' (الابن البار), but shares its spelling with the divine name البَرّ and with the loanword البار 'the bar'.
Human ('Magian/Zoroastrian') but almost entirely a sectarian slur in Gulf Twitter usage.
Orthographic duplicate of الاوروبي and الاروبي, both also in the inventory.
Hamza-variant duplicate of القاري (also in the inventory, mis-glossed there as 'villager').
Transliteration duplicate of البروفيسور (also in the inventory).
Archaic 'companion/consort'; low currency.
In modern usage denotes the bride (female); the 'bridegroom' gloss is the classical sense. Female referent.
Human ('well-mannered'); the CAMeL gloss 'educator' is misleading.
Collective plural 'riffraff/barbarians' — human referents, but plural and purely abusive.
Also a divine name and a family name; the human 'Quran memoriser / custodian' reading is live and frequent.
Human ('dancer', pejorative for a male dancer) but also 'pendulum'.
Denotes an unmarried woman past the usual age; female referent and a pejorative.
Human-applying participle 'present/on hand' but freely applied to objects; also widely considered a usage error for الموجود.
Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (Meccan; also modifies non-humans as in السور المكية).
Human ('counterpart') but heavily used in the idiom منقطع النظير.
Egyptian dialect 'the decent/stand-up guy'; human, colloquial.
Dialectal 'joker'; human, but the plural النكات 'the jokes' is a homograph.
Variant of الطاغية / الطاغيه (also in the inventory).
Rare classical 'deceiver'; low currency and easily confused with dialectal خب.
Human as 'the missing person' but equally applied to lost objects.
Elevated 'king': divine in classical religious texts, human in the Saudi anthem and royal panegyric (عاش المليك). Human reading retained but register-bound.

Family name and a famous drama title (رأفت الهجان), but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (camel rider/border camel corps).
The 'Hamite' gloss is academic; the live readings are the participle 'protector' (human) and 'hot' (non-human). Ambiguous but a human reading survives.
Denotes an Abbasid person, but dominant use is attributive (العصر/الخلافة العباسية); also a family name.
Human (pimp/cuckold); among the most vulgar Levantine-Egyptian insults.
Human ('officer in charge'); Egyptian administrative term, and the passive participle 'the one ordered'.
Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept ('pilot' is fully live).
Modern nationality form; الحبشي (also in the inventory) is the older/ethnic near-synonym.
Human (Byzantine/Roman) but dominantly the poet جلال الدين الرومي and the historical adjective; also a family name.
Human ('emperor') but also a common sports epithet.
Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (jeweller).
Rare ('toothless'); also the classical name الأهتم. Human but very low currency.
Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (oil/oilseed merchant).
Human ('complainant'); the CAMeL gloss 'defendant' is wrong (that is المشتكى عليه).
Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept ('barber' is fully live).
Dialectal 'salesman'; human, colloquial.
Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (shepherd).

Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept ('butcher'); the CAMeL gloss 'land surveyor' is wrong for modern usage.
Human singular of المرتزقة 'mercenary'; the CAMeL gloss 'means of subsistence' is the non-human homograph.
Classical/poetic variant of اليمني (also in the inventory); on Twitter also carries the eschatological figure اليماني.
Human (pimp/procurer); vulgar.
Human ('amputee') but also Quranic polemic (إن شانئك هو الأبتر) and 'docked' of animals.
Dialectal 'broke, penniless'; human but colloquial.
Human (a man complicit in his womenfolk's dishonour); vulgar religious insult.
Quranic epithet 'oft-repentant' (human referent) but confined to religious quotation.
Rare orthographic duplicate of الانجليزي / الانكليزي, both also in the inventory.
Human ('sponsor' in the Gulf kafala system); a legal role term, and also a divine-adjacent epithet in some religious usage.
Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (herbalist/perfumer, fully live in the Gulf and Egypt).
Denotes an Ottoman person, but dominant use is attributive (الدولة/الخلافة العثمانية); also a family name.
Human ('sitting companion'), literary/hadith register (الجليس الصالح).
Nationality term (Mongolian) but on Twitter mostly a slur for a person with Down syndrome; human but abusive.
Human (village headman); ta-marbuta form, Egyptian institutional term.
Literary adjective 'affable'; also a given name أنيس.
Human ('doer, perpetrator', فاعل خير) but also the grammatical term 'subject of a verb'.
Egyptian dialect 'the kid/child' (human); the CAMeL gloss 'family/household' reflects the classical collective sense.

Family name (علي الحجار), but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept ('stone mason' remains a recognised trade term).
Rare intensive adjective 'much-laughing'; human-applying but low currency.
Hamza-variant duplicate of المسئول (also in the inventory).
Chiefly the divine formula علام الغيوب; the human 'great expert' reading is weak.
Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (miller).
'Barren' — almost always predicated of a woman; female referent and highly marked.
Adjective 'cheerful, smiling'; human-applying, evaluative rather than referential.
Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (from Homs).
Levantine dialect 'the young guy'; also the homograph الشب 'alum'. Human, colloquial.
Used as an insult for a person, but the CAMeL gloss ('mean trick, infamy') shows an abstract reading is also live.

Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept ('butcher' is fully live, including as a political epithet).

Dominantly the Sufi al-Hallaj, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (cotton ginner) — weakest of this group.
Human as 'the one who caused it' but equally applied to non-human causes.
Human 'kinsman/in-law', but نسيب is also the amatory prelude of a qasida.
Human-applying ('outstanding', of players and performers) but formally just an adjective.
Human, dominantly the football full-back (الظهير الأيمن); the 'supporter' sense is literary.
Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept ('doorman' is fully live).
Human/team as 'the crowned champion'; often refers to a club rather than a person.
The CAMeL gloss 'critic' is wrong for modern usage: المعيب normally means 'shameful/defective' of an act or thing. Kept only because a 'faultfinder' reading is formally available.
Human ('diplomat') but also 'diplomatic' modifying missions and language.
Obsolete trade term 'soap boiler'; survives chiefly as a family name.
Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (veterinarian/farrier).
Denotes an Ayyubid person, but dominant reference is صلاح الدين الأيوبي; also a family name.
Orthographic duplicate of الانجليزي and الانقليزي, both also in the inventory.
Plural 'servants/domestic workers' — human, but plural.
Rare poetic 'swaggering'; also a given name.
Rare; effectively the literary الوديع 'gentle one'. The CAMeL gloss 'consignor' is legal jargon.
Human ('male nurse'); strongly gendered counterpart of the far more frequent الممرضة.
Human ('the reproacher') but confined to classical love poetry.

Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (from Mansoura). Wazn tag mu_participle is an error; it is a nisba.
Denotes a Fatimid person, but dominant use is attributive (الدولة الفاطمية); also a family name.
Human (university 'teaching assistant'); institutional jargon, and the participle 'the one who repeats'.
Human ('husband') only in classical/legal register; modern hits also include Baal and rain-fed agriculture (زراعة بعلية).
Human ('specialist') but also 'competent' of authorities and bodies (الجهة المختصة).
Chiefly شمس التبريزي; surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept is only weakly satisfied (from Tabriz).
Human in the dominant Twitter usage (slur for a homosexual person); the neutral 'anomalous' adjective also exists.
Misspelled duplicate of الاوروبي / الاوربي, both also in the inventory.
Non-standard spelling of الكازاخستاني 'Kazakhstani'. Human nationality nisba.
Human 'watchman' in Egyptian usage (خفير/غفير), but also the idiom الجم الغفير 'the multitude'.
Dialectal/classical 'repentant'; also the classical نديم 'drinking companion'. Human, marked register.
Obsolete trade term 'seed seller'; survives chiefly as the family name al-Bazzar (hadith transmitter).
Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (greengrocer).
Human ('the blamer') but literary/Quranic register (لومة لائم).
Obsolete trade term 'silk weaver'; survives chiefly as a family name.
Human ('seducer' or dialectal 'enthusiast/amateur'), but the two senses pull apart sharply by register.
Transliteration duplicate of البروفسور (also in the inventory).

Family name and clerical title (عبد المهدي الكربلائي); surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept weakly satisfied (from Karbala).
Literary adjective 'mild-mannered'; human-applying, low currency.
Human as 'editor' (the dominant reading); the CAMeL gloss 'written/booked' reflects the non-human passive participle.
Plural — either the historical 'clients/mawali' (human) or 'lords/masters' with divine overtones; plural and ambiguous.
Confessional/regional near-duplicate of البحريني (also in the inventory).

Family name, but surname test applied: the definite form still has a live, frequent common-noun use on Twitter beyond the family name, so kept (Jerusalemite); note the very frequent non-human الحديث القدسي.
Human ('shareholder') but also 'contributing' of factors, and الشركة المساهمة.
Human (Hebrew person) but dominant use modifies language and media (الموقع العبري، اللغة العبرية).
Human as 'the dominant one' but equally applied to teams, states and forces.
Quranic 'liar/conjecturer' (قتل الخراصون); human but confined to quotation.
